summary: Phase 135Q froze the Stage 2 ("Atomic Publication Rehearsal, Legacy Authority") contract and implementation plan for the CLTR migration, in docs/PHASE_135_ATOMIC_PUBLICATION_REHEARSAL_CONTRACT_AND_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md. This is an architecture, contract-freeze, and implementation-planning phase only -- no Stage 2 implementation, no rehearsal generation, no rehearsal pointer, no production pointer change, no authority cutover, and no legacy-authority demotion or retirement occurred. Independently reviewed CLTR-001, CLTR-SCHEMA-001 v1.0.1, 135D's temporal/state/representation models, 135H/135H.2's integration and recovery-hardening plans, 135J's schema verification, 135K/135L's shadow implementation and verification, 135M's migration/atomic-publication contract, 135N's migration-contract verification (including its resolution of transition_id design-B and its repair of the temporal-impossibility finding F-135N-1), 135O's Stage 1 shared transition-input and dual-derivation implementation, and 135P's independent Stage 1 verification, via a dedicated research pass reading primary documents and source rather than relying on phase summaries alone. Located and dispositioned all four exact 135P Non-Blocking findings (F-135P-1 through F-135P-4) with full component, atomicity, split-brain, recovery, and exactly-once relevance analysis, reclassifying F-135P-1 (entry-point recovery-classification wiring gap), F-135P-3 (derive_cltr crash on non-empty commit ownership), F-135P-4 (hardcoded non-authority disclosure constant), and the EXPECTED_REPRESENTATION_DIFFERENCE half of F-135P-2 (unreachable comparison classes) as Blocking prerequisites for Stage 2 implementation specifically -- not for this contract-freeze phase and not for continued Stage 1 operation. Froze: a Stage 2 authority matrix confirming legacy remains sole production authority throughout; a deterministic, retry-safe rehearsal-generation identity bound to migration epoch, authority epoch, transition ID, shared-input package ID, final input revision digest, phase/task identity, schema versions, rehearsal stage, and production-authority disclosure; an isolated .pcae/cltr-migration/epochs/<epoch>/rehearsals/ namespace as a sibling of Stage 1's existing transitions/ namespace, with explicit path-traversal, symlink-escape, and no-historical-rewrite containment rules; frozen candidate-versus-authoritative terminology (production authoritative artifact, rehearsal candidate artifact, copied evidence artifact, normalized legacy representation, CLTR-derived representation, external-effect intent, unverifiable artifact, projected artifact); a 23-item candidate artifact inventory with per-artifact contracts for the report, completion metadata, Architecture Status, checkpoint, notification-intent, marker, and receipt candidates, plus commit-attribution, repository-transition, and other representation adapters; a manifest and generation-digest contract with explicit algorithm identification and nested per-artifact digest binding; a deterministic 19-step candidate-assembly sequence; a precondition contract, a mismatch policy, an atomic non-authoritative rehearsal-pointer contract, an explicit atomicity-scope statement that does not overclaim multi-filesystem or external-service atomicity, filesystem assumptions stated honestly per platform, a full crash matrix across 17 crash points, a state-based (never inference-based) recovery contract, an idempotency contract, a conflicting-replay table, a quarantine contract, a rehearsal-comparison contract distinguishing expected rehearsal differences from fabricated matches, a progression-eligibility contract that remains advisory only, a Stage 2 evidence-record contract, read-only status and reconciliation command plans (not implemented), rollback-rehearsal and roll-forward guidance, a split-brain-prevention contract, identical treatment across all four production finalization entry points (task_finish, phase_complete, phase_report_create, notify_send_report), ordinary/recovery-path behavior, an explicit proof that a rejected 135H.1-style recovery candidate cannot satisfy Stage 2 preconditions or succeed as a rehearsal, exactly-once preservation, notification/marker/receipt isolation (no dispatch, no production marker or receipt mutation), a feature-configuration and invalid-configuration matrix using a new PCAE_CLTR_ATOMIC_REHEARSAL_ENABLED flag alongside the existing Stage 1 flags, a security/containment matrix, and an explicit no-execution-boundary restatement. Produced a planned package structure under src/pcae/cltr/migration/rehearsal/ (18 modules) following existing repository convention, integration-point plan tied to the exact point Stage 1's shared-input LEGACY_COMPLETION stage is already captured, a 23-module planned test suite, a fault-injection plan covering every candidate-assembly step, and explicit acceptance criteria. Compiled a full inherited-finding review (135P, 135N, 135J), a 17-row risk register, and a cross-reference matrix classifying every Stage 2 contract rule against CLTR-001, CLTR-SCHEMA-001, 135D, 135H, 135H.2, 135M, 135N, 135O, 135P, PFN-001, and PFR-001, with no unsupported semantic invention identified. No production source file under src/ was modified. No production test file was modified. Legacy lifecycle remains the sole production authority; CLTR remains derivative; runtime remains Observed / observe / execution unavailable. CLTR-001, CLTR-SCHEMA-001 v1.0.1, PFN-001, and PFR-001 all unchanged. Recommends 135R -- Atomic Publication Rehearsal Contract Verification (architecture/contract verification only; must precede any Stage 2 implementation).
